page: Microsoft Azure M16ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the MSMediumMemoryv4 series, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes a resource allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it in a high memory-to-core tier designed for working sets that exceed typical standard compute profiles.

Hardware integration excludes onboard local storage and discrete GPUs. Storage operations rely entirely on attached network-based storage, with support for Premium Storage tiers. Additionally, the instance configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The omission of local NVMe storage prioritizes memory allocation density while delegating disk persistence and I/O durability to external managed volumes.

Cost efficiency for this instance is characterized by its high memory density per compute unit, enabling operators to host high-memory workloads without over-provisioning unused CPU cores. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large relational databases, in-memory key-value caches, intermediate data manipulation pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring substantial memory footprints.
